profile.reading: This is Hetzners Data Center Park in Tuusula, north of Helsinki, Finland, at Huurrekuja 10, a multi building colocation and cloud hosting campus that has grown to house 14 individual data center buildings, numbered HEL1-DC1 through HEL1-DC14, all operated by German hosting company Hetzner. The Helsinki park became operational starting in 2018 with its first phase, and the campus overall is reported at 24 megawatts of power capacity. Hetzner Online, headquartered in Gunzenhausen, Germany, is one of Europes larger web hosting and cloud infrastructure providers, offering dedicated servers, cloud servers, colocation, and managed hosting to customers internationally, and holds ISO 27001 information security certification across its data center operations, including this Finnish site, which extended the companys infrastructure beyond its original German data centers into the Nordic market. Hetzner Online was founded in 1997 by electrical engineer Martin Hetzner in Gunzenhausen, growing from a small regional web host into one of Europes larger hosting groups, which converted from AG to GmbH corporate status in 2015 while remaining privately, founder controlled. Beyond Gunzenhausen and this Tuusula campus, Hetzner operates data centers in Falkenstein, Germany, opened 2009, Nuremberg, Germany, opened 2012, Ashburn, Virginia, opened 2021, Hillsboro, Oregon, opened 2022, and Singapore, opened 2024. By 2025 the company reported operating more than 500,000 server units and supporting more than one million active cloud instances simultaneously, up from roughly 200,000 hosted domains on 20,000 servers in 2008, with 2021 figures showing about 367 million euros in revenue and 103 million euros in net income. The Tuusula park was chosen in part for Finlands cool climate, which supports efficient free air cooling, and for the countrys renewable rich electricity grid.
